q.q: Rain washes trash and oil off a parking lot and into a storm drain. Where does that water usually go next?
o: Into creeks, rivers, lakes, and the ocean
Straight back up into the clouds
Into a cleaning plant every single time
Nowhere. It disappears into the ground right away.

q.q: A meadow full of wildflowers is paved over to make a parking lot. What most likely happens to the bees and rabbits that lived there?
o: They find more food on the warm pavement.
Nothing changes for them.
They lose food and shelter, so many must move or may not survive.
They turn into new kinds of animals.

q.q: Pollution can only harm water. It cannot get into the air or the land.
A thin, shiny film of oil is floating on a pond. Which cleanup tool would work best?
o: A fishing net
An absorbent pad that soaks up oil
A magnet
A garden rake
Using up natural resources as fast as possible
Studying the weather every day
Moving every wild animal into a zoo
Taking care of natural resources and habitats so they stay healthy and last

q.q: Bald eagles almost disappeared because a bug poison called DDT made their eggshells thin. What helped the eagles come back?
o: People banned DDT and protected eagle nests.
Eagles learned to lay eggs on the ground.
People fed the eagles bread.
The eagles moved to other countries.

q.q: Which of these are ways to save water? Choose ALL that are correct.
o: Fix a leaky faucet
Cover garden soil with mulch
Leave the sprinkler on while it rains
Catch rain in a rain barrel for the garden

q.q: Why do scientists say that reducing waste is even better than recycling?
o: Recycling makes more trash.
Reducing is only for grown-ups.
Reducing means less is used and thrown away in the first place.
Recycling never works.

q.q: A wetland has many different kinds of living things. One kind of bird disappears from it. What is most likely to happen?
o: The whole wetland falls apart right away.
Other living things fill in, and the wetland stays steadier than a place with only a few kinds.
Every other animal leaves too.
The wetland turns into a desert.

q.q: A student writes a plan to protect a park's birds. Which is the best criterion for success, something you can check?
o: "We want the park to be nice."
"Birds are important."
"Everyone should care about nature."
"The number of nesting birds goes up within two years."
